newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU Parliament condemns annulment of Serb elections.
newsitem.headline: EU Parliament condemns annulment of Serb elections.

text.p: The European Parliament on Wednesday condemned the Serbian authorities for annulling the results of November 17 local elections and urged the European Union not to offer Serbia preferential trade terms.

In a strongly-worded statement, the EU's directly-elected assembly expressed deep concern about developments in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, including the silencing of independent media and the overturning of election results.
The 626-member Parliament demanded that the Belgrade authorities respect the elections and launch a full inquiry into alleged irregularities in the poll.

The Euro-deputies' statement echoes a similar call from EU foreign ministers, who on December 6 postponed a decision to offer Serbia and Montenegro preferential trade terms already granted to other Balkan states.

Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring, who chaired the December 6 meeting, told Euro-MPs on Wednesday the ministers wanted the federal republic to rejoin the international community, "for the sake of prosperity and stability in the region".
"But it cannot do so unless it observes basic standards of democracy and human rights," he insisted.

In their resolution, which is non-binding, the Euro-MPs insisted that "counteracting developments towards democray -- of which free elections and a free media are a fundamental part -- cannot be accepted by the Union".

The EU should not develop closer relations with the republic until the Serbs helped apprehend indicted war criminals on their territory and acted to reduce tension over the Serb-governed Kosovo region, the EU Parliament said.
